changes: Arsenic permissible cell: 0.05 mg/L to no relaxation
Clause 4.1.1 bacteriology method: IS 1622 to IS 15185
Boron conditional permissible cell: 1.0 to 2.4 mg/L
Mineral oil acceptable cell: 0.5 to 1.0 mg/L
Add uranium 0.03 mg/L with no relaxation
Replace MS2 methods and distinguish subsequent investigation guidance
Replace sampling clause, including IS 15185 for bacteriology
Add referenced standards to Annex A; retain printed Part 65/Part 2 title discrepancy for method-document verification
Uranium method: IS 3025 Part 65* or IS 14194 Part 3
Add IS 14194 Part 3:2021 to Annex A

findings.title: Acceptable and conditional upper values
findings.detail: The higher permissible column is conditional on absence of an alternative source. Colour and sulphate add further conditions. It is not a routine substitute for the acceptable reference.

findings.title: Iron–manganese interpretation remains open
findings.detail: Amendment 1 changes the iron cell from 0.3 to 1.0 mg/L. The original Fe + Mn combined 0.3 mg/L remarks remain in the retrieved text; none of amendments 1–4 removes them. Both are retained for clarification.

findings.title: Residual chlorine is a minimum
findings.detail: The chlorinated-water row specifies a consumer-end minimum and a separate viral-protection minimum. Its second-column value is preserved as printed; the helper does not turn it into a general maximum.

findings.title: Uranium is separate from alpha/beta activity
findings.detail: Amendment 3 adds uranium to Table 3 at 0.03 mg/L without relaxation. Amendment 4 changes its method options. It is not automatically removed by the ingredient-water FAQ radioactive-parameter wording; that applicability question requires confirmation.

findings.title: Methods and sample volumes matter
findings.detail: Amendments 2–3 update bacteriology to IS 15185 and distinguish operative MS2 requirements from guidance clauses. The eight microbial/biological entries retain 100 mL, 1 L and 10 L sample bases and their water-system scopes.

findings.title: Document dates take precedence in this reference
findings.detail: The BIS page lists amendment 3 under 2020, but the downloaded amendment heading reads February 2021. Amendment 4 is headed November 2021. The earlier metadata inventory is retained as history, not used as the amendment text date.

The earlier full-text retrieval gap is resolved. Conditional upper values, microbial sample volumes and the iron–manganese interpretation hold remain explicit.

rows.name: Colour
rows.scopeNote: Conditional upper value requires absence of an alternative source and no suspected toxic substances.

rows.name: Odour
rows.scopeNote: Assess cold/heated and at several dilutions.

rows.name: pH
rows.scopeNote: No broader range inferred.

rows.name: Taste
rows.scopeNote: Taste examination only after safety is established.

rows.name: Free residual chlorine
rows.scopeNote: Only for chlorinated water, at the consumer end. The row is a minimum: 0.2 mg/L, or 0.5 mg/L when viral protection is required. The other column prints 1; it is not turned into a generic maximum rule.

rows.name: Iron as Fe
rows.scopeNote: Amendment 1 changes the iron cell to 1.0 mg/L but the base remarks still specify combined Fe + Mn at most 0.3 mg/L. The retrieved amendments do not remove that remark. Keep this interpretation hold.

rows.name: Manganese as Mn
rows.scopeNote: The base remarks retain combined Fe + Mn at most 0.3 mg/L; assess with the iron amendment and do not clear this row in isolation.

rows.name: Mineral oil
rows.methodReference: IS 3025 Part 39 clause 6, infrared partition method

rows.name: Sulphate as SO4
rows.scopeNote: The 400 mg/L conditional upper value also requires magnesium at most 30 mg/L.

rows.name: Pesticides
rows.scopeNote: Pointer only, not an additional pesticide limit or a total-pesticide default.

rows.name: Total arsenic as As
rows.scopeNote: Amendment 1 removes the older 0.05 mg/L relaxation.

methodNotes.tables2And3: Amendment 3 permits approved and validated international methods from ISO, APHA, ASTM, AOAC, EPA and EN. For disputes, the listed column-5 methods and starred referee methods apply. Current editions and laboratory validation remain to be checked.
methodNotes.table5: The source methods guide the laboratory; where two methods are given, USEPA is the reference method.
methodNotes.sampling: Amendment 3 retains IS 1622 and IS 3025 Part 1 for representative sampling and specifies IS 15185 for bacteriological sampling.
